“This is not just about an NFL comeback, it’s for the people out there that’s struggling…that don’t want to wake up, that want to commit suicide, that have suicide ideations, that are on a manic phase right now……It’s for G@d damn sure not who I want my kids to be, I don’t want my kids to be running off in the streets. I want my kids to respectable men that people love…This is about teaching my kids that hey--no matter where you are in life, this is how you go get it...."

title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 1: - First off, a quick reminder that pads won't come on for a few days so a little bit of a caveat on all things until we get to the real stuff. - Coach Kyle Shanahan came out to the field after a couple of team periods and stood by GM John Lynch for much of the next half hour or so. Shanahan was wearing sunglasses to cover the black eyes he has from his accident with LB Fred Warner complimenting him on his "disguise." Warner, FB Kyle Juszczyk and LB Dre Greenlaw all came out to greet Shanahan during a special teams period with Shanahan heading back inside before practice ended. - The only player not participating to start the roughly 90-minute session was DB Nate Hobbs. title: Crisp first training camp practice for the 49ers. Some highlights, including... 🏈a Brock Purdy deep heave to Mike Evans, big gain 🏈Malik Mustapha explosive PBU against Ricky Pearsall on another great ball from Purdy 🏈De'Zhaun Stribling made a couple nice catches, including one on a deep out and then one down the seam to close practice 🏈Fred Warner swarmed in for a "welcome back" tackle on Play 3 — was fired up 🏈CMC beat Romello Height, who was dropping in coverage as part of Raheem Morris' new defensive look, with nifty cutback in the flat 🏈CMC, with a lot of juice to open camp, also later caught a pass against the much smaller Upton Stout 🏈Jalen Graham INT off Mac Jones, which came off a Garret Wallow tip 🏈Kyle Shanahan half-hour cameo
summary:
Crisp first training camp practice for the 49ers. Some highlights, including...

🏈a Brock Purdy deep heave to Mike Evans, big gain
🏈Malik Mustapha explosive PBU against Ricky Pearsall on another great ball from Purdy
🏈De'Zhaun Stribling made a couple nice catches, including one on a deep out and then one down the seam to close practice
🏈Fred Warner swarmed in for a "welcome back" tackle on Play 3 — was fired up
🏈CMC beat Romello Height, who was dropping in coverage as part of Raheem Morris' new defensive look, with nifty cutback in the flat
🏈CMC, with a lot of juice to open camp, also later caught a pass against the much smaller Upton Stout
🏈Jalen Graham INT off Mac Jones, which came off a Garret Wallow tip
🏈Kyle Shanahan half-hour cameo
full_text:
Crisp first training camp practice for the 49ers. Some highlights, including...

🏈Malik Mustapha explosive PBU against Ricky Pearsall on another great ball from Purdy
🏈De'Zhaun Stribling made a couple nice catches, including one on a deep out and then one down the seam to close practice
🏈Fred Warner swarmed in for a "welcome back" tackle on Play 3 — was fired up
🏈CMC beat Romello Height, who was dropping in coverage as part of Raheem Morris' new defensive look, with nifty cutback in the flat
🏈CMC, with a lot of juice to open camp, also later caught a pass against the much smaller Upton Stout

title: One important nugget on Foster Griffin.. If the Nationals were to keep him and then offer him a qualifying offer and he turned it down and left in free agency, they would get a compensatory draft pick just after the second round. Valuable asset for a team that prides itself on draft and development. Plenty of talent to be found in that range; significantly boosts pool money to be spread around in the draft. This doesn’t mean they will definitely keep him. But I do think it makes it more stomachable to retain him even if he might walk. Nats can hold out for a better prospect return than whatever level of player they anticipate drafting in the 50s.

summary:
49ers GM John Lynch doesn’t think Kyle Shanahan’s injuries will prevent him from coaching the Sept. 10 regular-season opener against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
 
“That’s not what we’re anticipating,” Lynch said. “That’s not what I’ve  heard from the doctors. But just like we talked about with players, the timeline kind of takes care of itself. He’s got to meet certain markers. But I think the expectation is that long before that he’ll be better.”
full_text:
49ers GM John Lynch doesn’t think Kyle Shanahan’s injuries will prevent him from coaching the Sept. 10 regular-season opener against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
